title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's mathematics. It is page -4- of a typescript, scanned upside down, of R. Steinberg's 'Regular elements of semisimple algebraic groups' (Publ. Math. IHÉS 25, 1965), from the introduction. Grothendieck evidently used the blank backs of this preprint as scrap paper for his 1965 manuscript notes on Frobenius eigenvalues and motivic Galois groups over F_q (see the neighbouring pages).

The content in modern terms:
- G is a semisimple algebraic group over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, of rank r.
- N is the 'Steinberg cross-section' of the regular conjugacy classes. It is built as a product of root subgroups U_{α_i} times representatives n_{s_i} of the simple reflections, attached to a Coxeter element.
- §7.4: for SL(r+1), N gives the companion-matrix (rational canonical) normal form of a regular matrix. This suggests the problem of extending normal forms to non-regular elements.
- §7.1: N is closed, irreducible and isomorphic to affine r-space V.
- §7.9 (main lemma): if G is simply connected, the map x ↦ (χ_1(x),…,χ_r(x)), given by the fundamental characters, restricts to an isomorphism N → A^r. This is the Steinberg map G → G//G ≅ A^r, and N is a section of it.
- Theorem 1.5: for simply connected G, x is regular iff the differentials dχ_i are linearly independent at x.
- The page then compares with Kostant's Lie-algebra analogues: the Kostant slice and the regularity criterion via the differentials of the basic invariants u_i, over C or any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0. It remarks that the group characters are more tractable than the u_i, so the group proofs work in all characteristics.
errors: No mathematical errors. 'among other thing' is a typo in the original typescript (should be 'things'). Theorem 1.5 and the Steinberg section results are correct and well known.

ideas.what: Cross-section N of regular classes, isomorphic to A^r, mapped isomorphically onto A^r by the fundamental characters (G simply connected)
ideas.modern_name: Steinberg cross-section / Steinberg slice; Steinberg map G → T/W ≅ A^r

ideas.what: Regularity criterion: x is regular iff dχ_1,…,dχ_r are independent at x
ideas.usually_credited_to: R. Steinberg (1965); Lie algebra analogue by B. Kostant (1963)
ideas.where_published: Steinberg 1965, Theorem 1.5; Kostant, Amer. J. Math. 85 (1963)

ideas.what: Companion-matrix normal form for SL(r+1) as a special case of N
ideas.modern_name: Rational canonical form for regular elements

missed.claim: This archival page is a verso of Steinberg's 1965 IHÉS preprint, reused by Grothendieck for his motivic Galois/Frobenius-eigenvalue notes. This dates the material and shows that Grothendieck had Steinberg's preprint at hand. It is a provenance detail only; there is no new mathematics by Grothendieck here.
missed.quote: 1.5 Theorem. If G is simply connected, the element x is regular if and only if the differentials dX_i are independent at x.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only for archival cataloguing and dating: it is evidence that the manuscript notes in cote 15 date from around 1965, written on IHÉS preprint paper.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript of Steinberg's published 1965 paper, used as scrap paper. It contains no Grothendieck mathematics, and its content is fully published and credited.
transcription_corrections: The page image is rotated 180°; the text is Steinberg's typescript, not Grothendieck's.
The fundamental characters are typed as 'X_i' in the typescript but denote χ_i in Steinberg's paper.
'among other thing' is as in the original (typo for 'things').
The handwritten archive folio number in the corner (appears as '86' when rotated) is not part of the text.
